cases.title: Cables
cases.note: Golden Gate teaching model. Exercise is an adaptation of UE3 task 1b, q=20 kN/m.
cases.instruction: Draw a cable shape and its force diagram.

cases.title: Arches
cases.note: Representative Gothic section, not a measured analysis of Beauvais.
cases.instruction: Complete the side vaults and buttresses; draw the compression paths.

cases.title: Trusses
cases.note: Representative planar truss model, not a full Pompidou analysis.
cases.instruction: Find support reactions and construct the member forces.

cases.title: Beams
cases.note: Beam with overhang; generic beam teaching model.
cases.instruction: Draw the internal force flow and find support reactions.

cases.title: Frames
cases.note: Tagliamento bridge photo and corresponding frame model.
cases.instruction: Construct a force path through the frame and close the force diagram.

cases.title: Plates and slabs
cases.note: Slab force-flow model; exercise generalises load transfer to supporting beams.
cases.instruction: Trace the slab loads through the beams to the supports.

cases.title: Shells and vaults
cases.instruction: Draw the vault compression paths and find the tie forces.
cases.note: Representative barrel-vault strip model. Worksheet uses a tied masonry vault under self-weight.

cases.title: Columns
cases.note: Eccentric compression force flow; buckling exercise requires stability analysis in addition to equilibrium.
cases.instruction: Determine the buckling length for each support condition.

cases.title: Bracing
cases.note: House R128 X-bracing model; exercise considers equivalent bracing walls and slab.
cases.instruction: Transfer the horizontal load through the walls to the supports.

cases.title: Material-specific forms
cases.note: Gym Vrin timber arch-cable force model. Exercise compares cantilever forms in timber, concrete and steel.
cases.instruction: Compare the required cantilever depth in timber, concrete and steel.

cases.title: Plastic and stress-field models
cases.note: Palestra Doppia photo with a representative reinforced-concrete strut-and-tie / continuous stress-field comparison. Beam-opening exercise asks for admissible internal force paths; equilibrium alone does not establish plastic capacity.
cases.instruction: Draw strut-and-tie force paths around the openings.
